walkthroughs.body_html:
Light travels in straight lines, so when an opaque object blocks it, the area behind has no light - a shadow.

A bigger object or closer light makes a bigger shadow.

Eclipses are giant shadows: the Moon's shadow on Earth (solar eclipse) or Earth's shadow on the Moon (lunar eclipse).

Refraction is when light bends as it enters a new medium (like water or glass).

Going from air to water: light slows down and bends towards the normal.

This is why a straw in a glass of water looks broken at the surface.

Refraction also lets lenses focus light in glasses, cameras, and your eye!

White light is a mix of 7 colours: Red, Orange, Yellow, Green, Blue, Indigo, Violet.

A prism splits white light into this spectrum - because each colour refracts by a slightly different amount.

Rainbows form when sunlight hits water droplets - they act like millions of tiny prisms.
